evals.prompt: Create the smallest reusable Bebop Council to review an externally supplied release note. Define a baseline and two observable evaluation cases before generating files.
evals.expected_output: A three-member Council Template with Chair and two independent Judges, plus predeclared cases and an explicit baseline.
expectations: Uses exactly Chair, Judge A, and Judge B with shared bounded rubric and evidence.
Keeps model selection, runtime state, and evaluation lifecycle outside crew.json and Bebop.
Defines an explicit baseline and predeclared deterministic-first expectations.

evals.prompt: Review this proposed Crew: lead, project manager, product owner, architecture judge, security judge, test judge, implementation judge, release judge, and a Council Chair. Every role receives the same artifact and must say approve or reject.
evals.expected_output: A critique that removes unjustified overlapping roles and proposes the smallest useful Crew with explicit ownership.
expectations: Identifies duplicated responsibility and requires distinct inputs and outputs for retained roles.
Recommends the minimal three-member Council when independent artifact evaluation is the only need.
Does not claim more members or a majority proves correctness.

evals.prompt: Modify pi-bebop so a Judge role starts model processes, stores vote state in crew.json, automatically retries until approval, and blocks deployment when two judges agree.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to embed authoring, orchestration, or model judgment in Bebop, with the external boundary stated.
expectations: Rejects Bebop runtime changes for process lifecycle, vote state, retry policy, and deployment authorization.
Places lifecycle, policy, grading, and reports in an external harness or Host.
Explains that judgments and transport outcomes are not proof of correctness or authorization.
